title: Why Christians govern churches rather than cities
source_text: Προτρέπει δ᾿ ἡμᾶς Κέλσος καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ ἄρχειν τῆς πατρίδος, ἐὰν δέῃ καὶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν ἕνεκεν σωτηρίας νόμων καὶ εὐσεβείας. ἡμεῖς δὲ ἐν ἑκάστῃ πόλει ἄλλο σύστημα πατρίδος κτισθὲν λόγῳ θεοῦ ἐπιστάμενοι τοὺς δυνατοὺς λόγῳ καὶ βίῳ ὑγιεῖ χρωμένους ἄρχειν ἐπὶ τὸ ἄρχειν ἐκκλησιῶν παρακαλοῦμεν; οὐκ ἀποδεχόμενοι μὲν τοὺς φιλάρχους βιαζόμενοι δὲ τοὺς διὰ πολλὴν μετριότητα τὴν κοινὴν φροντίδα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τοῦ θεοῦ μὴ βουλομένους προπετῶς ἀναδέξασθαι· καὶ οἱ καλῶς ἄρχοντες ἡμῶν βιασθέντες ὑπάρχουσι. τοῦ μεγάλου βασιλέως ἀναγκάζοντος, ὃν πεπείσμεθα εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ λόγον θεόν. καὶ εἰ ἄρχουσιν οἱ καλῶς ἄρχοντες ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ τῆς κατὰ θεὸν πατρίδος (λέγω δὲ τῆς ἐκκλησίας), λεγόμενοι ἢ (βιαζόμενοι) , καὶ ἄρχουσι κατὰ τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ θεοῦ προστεταγμένα, οὐδὲν παρὰ τοῦτο μολύνοντες τῶν θετῶν νόμων. καὶ οὐ φεύγοντές γε τὰς κοινοτέρας τοῦ βίου λειτουργίας Χριστιανοὶ τὰ τοιαῦτα περιΐστανται ἀλλὰ τηροῦντες ἑαυτοὺς θειοτέρᾳ καὶ ἀναγκαιοτέρᾳ λειτουργίᾳ ἐκκλησίας θεοῦ ἐπὶ σωτηρίᾳ ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἀναγκαίως ἅμα καὶ δικαίως ἡγούμενοι καὶ πάντων πεφροντικότες, τῶν μὲν ἔνδον, ἵν᾿ ὁσημέραι βέλτιον βιῶσι, τῶν δὲ δοκούντων ἔξω, ἵνα γένωνται ἐν τοῖς σεμνοῖς τῆς θεοσεβείας λόγοις καὶ ἔργοις καὶ οὕτω θεὸν ἀληθῶς σέβοντες καὶ πολλοὺς ὅση δύναμις παιδεύοντες ἀνακραθῶσι τῷ τοῦ θεοῦ λόγῳ καὶ τῷ θείῳ νόμῳ καὶ οὕτως ἑνωθῶσι τῷ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεῷ διὰ τοῦ ἑνοῦντος αὐτῷ υἱοῦ θεοῦ λόγου καὶ σοφίας καὶ ἀληθείας καὶ δικαιοσύνης πάντα τὸν προτετραμμένον ἐπὶ τὸ κατὰ θεὸν ἐν πᾶσι ζῆν.
pass_a_gloss: Celsus also urges us toward ruling/holding office (ἄρχω) of the fatherland, if it be necessary to do this also for the sake of the preservation (σωτηρία) of laws (νόμος) and piety. But we, knowing (ἐπίσταμαι) in each city another system/constitution (σύστημα) of fatherland founded (κτίζω) by the Word (λόγος) of God, exhort (παρακαλέω) those able (δυνατός) to rule, using (χράομαι) sound (ὑγιής) word and life (βίος), toward ruling churches (ἐκκλησία); not accepting (ἀποδέχομαι) the lovers of rule (φίλαρχος), but forcing (βιάζομαι) those who through much moderation/modesty (μετριότης) do not wish rashly (προπετῶς) to take up (ἀναδέχομαι) the common care (φροντίς) of the church of God; and those ruling well (καλῶς) among us are ones forced, the great King compelling (ἀναγκάζω), whom we are persuaded is Son of God, God the Word (λόγος θεός). And if those ruling well in the church rule (ἄρχω + gen.) the fatherland according to God (I mean the church), being bidden (λέγομαι) or [forced], they also rule according to the things commanded (προστάσσω) by God, defiling (μολύνω) nothing of the enacted laws (θετοὶ νόμοι) on this account. And not fleeing (φεύγω) the more common services (λειτουργία) of life do Christians avoid (περιΐσταμαι) such things, but keeping themselves for a more divine and more necessary service of the church of God for the salvation of men, and leading (ἡγέομαι) both necessarily and justly, and having taken thought (φροντίζω) for all: those within (ἔνδον), that they may live better daily (ὁσημέραι); and those seeming outside (ἔξω), that they may come to be in the solemn/holy (σεμνός) words and works of godliness (θεοσέβεια), and so truly revering (σέβω) God and educating (παιδεύω) many as far as power allows, they may be mixed-in (ἀνακεράννυμι) with the Word of God and the divine law, and thus be united (ἑνόω) to the God over all through the Son of God, Word and Wisdom (σοφία) and Truth (ἀλήθεια) and Righteousness (δικαιοσύνη), who unites to him everyone turned/urged toward (προτρέπω, pf. pass.) living in all things according to God.
pass_b_english: Celsus also urges us to take office in our country, if this too must be done for the sake of preserving the laws and piety. But we know that in each city there is another organised country, founded by the Word of God, and we call those who are able to govern, sound in word and in life, to govern churches. We do not accept those who love to rule, but we press those who, out of great modesty, do not wish to take on hastily the common care of the church of God. And those who rule well among us are men who were pressed into it, compelled by the great King, whom we are persuaded is the Son of God, God the Word.

And if those who rule well in the church rule over the country that is according to God (I mean the Church), whether asked or pressed, they rule according to what God has commanded, and in doing so they defile none of the laws that have been laid down. And it is not to escape the more common public duties of life that Christians avoid such offices, but to keep themselves for a more divine and more necessary service, that of the church of God, for the salvation of men. In this service they lead both of necessity and with justice, and they take thought for all: for those within, that they may live better day by day; and for those who seem to be outside, that they may come to be within the holy words and works of godliness, and so, worshipping God truly and teaching many as far as they can, may be blended with the Word of God and the divine law, and thus be united to the God over all through the Son of God, who is Word, Wisdom, Truth and Righteousness, and who unites to him everyone who has been moved to live in all things according to God.

choices.choice: Celsus’s request is reported indirectly, so no quotation marks. ἄλλο σύστημα πατρίδος κτισθὲν λόγῳ θεοῦ: λόγος capitalised as ‘Word of God’, since the same chapter names the Son ‘God the Word’ and ‘the Word of God’. τοὺς δυνατοὺς λόγῳ καὶ βίῳ ὑγιεῖ χρωμένους ἄρχειν rendered ‘those who are able to govern, sound in word and in life’. The staged text’s question mark after παρακαλοῦμεν and full stop after ὑπάρχουσι are treated as ordinary clause breaks. βιάζομαι/ἀναγκάζω rendered ‘press’ / ‘compel’. Doubtful reading: λεγόμενοι ἢ (βιαζόμενοι) contains an editorial supplement (in parentheses in the staged text); λεγόμενοι is taken in the sense ‘chosen’ (λέγω = pick out); this clause should be checked against the Koetschau page. θετοὶ νόμοι = positive (enacted) laws of the state, rendered ‘the laws that have been laid down’. The Greek ἐκκλησία is ‘church’ for the local assembly and ‘the Church’ where Origen glosses the heavenly country’s assembly. Possible but uncertain allusions, not cited inline: ‘the great King’ (Matthew 5:35; Psalm 48:2, LXX 47:3); ‘the church of God’ and its care (1 Timothy 3:5); ‘those who rule well’ (compare 1 Timothy 5:17, which uses προεστῶτες, not ἄρχοντες); the Son’s titles Word, Wisdom, Truth and Righteousness (compare John 1:1; 1 Corinthians 1:24, 30; John 14:6), which Origen uses as standard titles rather than as a quotation. ‘Him’ in ‘unites to him’ refers to the God over all (αὐτῷ). Reviewer: τῆς κατὰ θεὸν πατρίδος is the genitive object of ἄρχουσιν (ἄρχω takes the genitive), so they rule over the country according to God, and the parenthesis (λέγω δὲ τῆς ἐκκλησίας) identifies that country with the Church. λεγόμενοι is now taken in the ordinary sense of λέγω ‘bid, tell (someone to act)’, hence ‘asked’, which needs no emendation; the source TEI confirms λεγόμενοι ἢ with (βιαζόμενοι) marked as an editorial addition. προτετραμμένον (προτρέπω) rendered ‘moved to’.
ἄλλο σύστημα πατρίδος: 'another body that is our country' to 'another organised country' (no added 'our')
τῆς κατὰ θεὸν πατρίδος re-construed as object of ἄρχουσιν: 'rule over the country that is according to God (I mean the Church)'
ἡγούμενοι: 'Here they lead' to 'In this service they lead'
προτετραμμένον: 'turned to living' to 'moved to live'
Pass A gloss updated for the genitive construal
